title: Cartwise Shopper Payouts Negative Balance and Freeze Limits
content:
## Payments Risk limits sheet — Cartwise Shopper Payouts

The unpaid earnings balance of a payout account may fall below zero when tip reductions or pay reversals arrive after money has been paid out. The sheet below sets, per plan, how far below zero the balance may go before the account is frozen, how the negative balance is recovered, and the freeze settings.

| Plan | Negative balance limit (USD below zero) | Recovery method | Share of each new credit applied to recovery | A returned deposit or cashout freezes the account until the destination is replaced | Target to decide a fraud-review freeze (business days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Weekly Direct Deposit | 25.00 | Offset against the next earnings | 100% | Yes | 5 |
| Instant Cashout | 25.00 | Offset against the next earnings | 100% | Yes | 5 |
| Everyday Pay Card Blue | 50.00 | Offset against the next earnings | 100% | Yes | 5 |
| Everyday Pay Card Gold | 50.00 | Offset against the next earnings | 100% | Yes | 3 |
| Everyday Pay Card Platinum | 75.00 | Offset against the next earnings | 100% | Yes | 3 |
| Everyday Pay Card Diamond | 100.00 | Offset against the next earnings | 100% | Yes | 2 |

### Limit readings (hypothetical balances)

The limit marks the most negative balance the account may carry; a balance more negative than minus the limit is beyond it.

| Plan (limit) | Hypothetical balance | Beyond the limit |
|---|---|---|
| Instant Cashout (25.00) | minus 25.00 | No — exactly at the limit |
| Instant Cashout (25.00) | minus 25.01 | Yes |
| Everyday Pay Card Platinum (75.00) | minus 60.00 | No |
| Everyday Pay Card Diamond (100.00) | minus 100.01 | Yes |

With a recovery share of 100% on every plan, each new credit is applied in full to the negative balance until it is recovered. Hypothetical: a balance of minus 18.00 followed by a credit of 30.00 leaves a balance of 12.00.
